key_concepts: A solution is a homogeneous mixture of solute and solvent
Soluble substances dissolve; insoluble substances do not
Solubility is the ability of a substance to dissolve in a solvent
Similar solute and solvent nature favors dissolving
Dissolving and melting are distinct processes
Higher temperature speeds up dissolving and melting
Increased temperature raises kinetic energy of particles
Concentration measures amount of solute in a given amount of solution
Percent by mass and percent by volume express concentration quantitatively
Saturated, unsaturated, and supersaturated solutions differ in amount of dissolved solute
Solubility curves predict solution type from solute and solvent amounts
Adding solvent dilutes a solution without changing solute mass
